N-main.objects: The statement itself gives real blocks A, B, C, constructs the symmetric block matrix M and defines the residual matrix S. No remote formula is needed.
N-main.domain: The integers p,q are at least one and each block dimension is explicit; vectors in the positivity definition have the appropriate real dimension.
N-main.fixed_and_variable: A,B,C are arbitrary fixed input blocks satisfying the stated assumptions. The positivity tests quantify varying vectors, not a solution matrix to be found.
N-main.hypotheses: A and C are symmetric and A has strictly positive quadratic form on every nonzero x. The hypothesis implies existence of A inverse through the zero-kernel argument developed in section 2.
N-main.equations: Both M=[[A,B],[B^T,C]] and S=C-B^T A^{-1}B are displayed inside the imported statement. The surrounding proof uses exactly those signs and block orders.
N-main.quantifiers: The criterion holds for each admissible block triple and all p,q>=1. Necessity tests each nonzero y separately; it does not select just one favourable y.
N-main.conclusion: Under the retained A>0 assumption the conclusion is precisely M positive definite if and only if S positive definite. Neither singular blocks nor a semidefinite extension is asserted.
N-main.status: This is an established elementary classical criterion, rederived as a lecture. The ending explicitly disclaims an originality claim.
N-main.local_definitions: Positive definite is defined within the statement, including the nonzero-vector quantifier. The only other operations are ordinary real transpose, multiplication and inverse, calibrated in section 1.

N-main: Expand the square with A symmetric and invertible.
Use the invertible change of variables for sufficiency.
Choose x=-A^{-1}By for every nonzero y to prove necessity.

findings: Reread the isolated canonical criterion. Its A>0 hypothesis simultaneously gives a zero kernel and the sign of z^T A z; the inverse therefore has a justified domain.
Recomputed z^T A z with (A^{-1})^T=A^{-1}; the cross terms agree as transposed real scalars and the remainder has minus B^T A^{-1}B, with all dimensions compatible.
Checked the inverse map by both compositions. Under A>0 and S>0, a nonzero pair gives either a positive z term or, if z=0, a positive y term.
Checked necessity with arbitrary nonzero y and x=-A^{-1}By. The pair stays nonzero and cancels the square, proving a universal positivity condition.
